Arkansas Landlord Tenant Law and Tenant Rights: Rules for Selling a Rental

Cash Home Buyers in Arkansas

  • Inherited, behind on payments, tenants, repairs: we buy it as-is
  • Zero fees, zero commissions, zero closing costs
  • No obligation: turn the offer down and owe us nothing

Selling a Arkansas House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is. Tell us about the property and the timeline.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from Arkansas statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we do not state it.

Arkansas statutes set the basic rules between landlords and tenants, including deposits, notices and what happens when a rental is sold. Here is what the official sources say.

What the official sources say

  • Security deposit may not exceed two months' rent; the AG notes the security-deposit law applies only to landlords who rent six or more units. (Arkansas Attorney General, Landlord And Tenant Rights (security deposits); source)
  • Landlord must return the deposit within 60 days after the tenant moves out and, if deducting, provide a written itemized list of charges within 60 days of vacating; entire deposit may be withheld if damages or unpaid rent exceed it. (Arkansas Attorney General, Landlord And Tenant Rights; source)
  • Landlord must give notice of at least one rental period before raising rent, for oral and written leases. (Arkansas Attorney General, Landlord And Tenant Rights; source)
  • A landlord may give notice of lease termination for any reason: one rental period's notice for an oral lease, or notice per the terms of a written lease. (Arkansas Attorney General, Landlord And Tenant Rights; source)
  • AG states Arkansas laws on these issues apply only to private rental units, not government-subsidized housing. (Arkansas Attorney General, Landlord And Tenant Rights; source)
Selling in Arkansas?
We buy Arkansas houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What we could not confirm

  • Details we could not confirm on an official page are not stated here. Read the statute sections linked above for the full text, and confirm deadlines with the court or county office.

How to sell a Arkansas house when this applies to you

  1. Write down who is in the house and on what terms: owner, heirs, tenants or occupants with no lease.
  2. Ask the title company what it needs to insure the sale, such as a recorded deed, court papers or a payoff letter.
  3. Get the payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the proceeds at closing.
  4. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. See we buy houses in Arkansas.

What a cash sale of a Arkansas house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in Arkansas.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.
  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.
  3. Pick your closing date. You choose the timeline. Some owners need weeks to move out, and others want to close quickly.
  4. The title company handles the paperwork. It checks ownership, pays off any mortgage and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds, and records the deed.
  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

Documents and information to have ready

You do not need everything below to get an offer, but each item makes the sale smoother and helps the title company work faster.

  • The deed or other proof of who owns the property today.
  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing, selling it yourself or a cash offer: how they compare

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required Arkansas disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

Questions to ask before you sell in Arkansas

  • Ask the title company what is owed and what the title company will need at closing.
  • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.
  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

These are general questions to start a conversation, not legal advice. Rules in Arkansas change, so confirm details with the official office or a Arkansas attorney or tax professional.

More questions about selling in Arkansas

How fast can I close on a cash sale?

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

Do I have to clean out or repair the house?

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Will you buy a house that has tenants in it?

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease when you request an offer.

What if I owe more on the mortgage than the house is worth?

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

Is there any cost to request an offer?

No. Requesting an offer is free and carries no obligation.

Arkansas Landlord Tenant Law and Tenant Rights FAQ

Can I sell my Arkansas rental with a tenant living in it?

Yes. A rental can be sold occupied. What happens to the lease depends on its terms and the statutes cited above.

Do I have to return the security deposit when I sell?

The deposit rules in the sources above still apply. Ask the title company how the deposit will be transferred or credited at closing.

Will you buy a house with tenants who are behind on rent?

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease and payment history when you request an offer.

Arkansas law requires a landlord to give a specific written notice before filing an eviction, and the number of days depends on the reason. Here is what the official sources say.

What the official sources say

  • Nonpayment of rent: landlord must give three days' written notice to vacate; if tenant does not leave, landlord sues by complaint in court (unlawful detainer). (Arkansas Attorney General, Landlord And Tenant Rights; source)
  • After service of summons, tenant has five days to object in writing filed with the court clerk; if no objection, the county sheriff can remove the tenant; if objection, a hearing is scheduled. (Arkansas Attorney General, Landlord And Tenant Rights; source)
  • No-cause termination: one rental period's notice for an oral lease, or as the written lease provides. (Arkansas Attorney General, Landlord And Tenant Rights; source)

Arkansas Tax Deed and Tax Lien Sales: Process, Redemption and Selling First

Cash Home Buyers in Arkansas
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Inherited, behind on payments, tenants, repairs: we buy it as-is
  • Zero fees, zero commissions, zero closing costs
  • No obligation: turn the offer down and owe us nothing

We buy as-is. Tell us about the property and the timeline.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from Arkansas statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we do not state it.

When property tax goes unpaid in Arkansas, the statutes allow the taxing authority to sell a lien or the property itself, and they give the owner a set time to redeem. Here is what the official sources say.

What the official sources say

  • Sale date must be no earlier than one year after the tax-delinquent parcel is certified to the Commissioner of State Lands. (26 CAR 400-104; source)
  • Until the parcel is sold or disposed of by the state, a person may redeem by petition to the Commissioner plus payment of outstanding taxes, penalties, interest, fees and costs; effective July 1, 2023 petitions and payment must be received before 4:00 p.m. CT on the last business day before the auction; partial payments do not extend redemption. (26 CAR 400-108; source)
  • Money from a tax-delinquent sale above taxes, fees, penalties, interest and costs is excess proceeds, distributed on application per statute (Ark. Code 26-37-205); any remainder is held in trust by the Commissioner of State Lands for the former owner. (26 CAR 400-401; source)

Can I sell my Arkansas house before a tax sale?

Yes. The unpaid tax, interest and costs are paid from the sale proceeds at closing, which stops the tax sale.

Only within the redemption rules in the statutes cited above. Check the deadline with the county office that ran the sale.

Yes. We buy as-is and the title company pays the tax from the proceeds at closing.
